items.title: Interview #100 Peter Evans, CEO at Xtract One Technologies
items.summary: Peter Evans, CEO at Xtract One Technologies, breaks down why many AI weapons scanners at school and stadium entrances still measure the wrong things. He explains why most "AI-enabled" detectors rest on the same physics as a walk-through metal detector, why knives and laptops expose the limits of that physics, and why a claim of 3,000 people an hour means little if a weak model sends most of them to a bag check. Peter also dives into how to estimate the weapons a system misses when nobody reports them, who should own the sensitivity dial, and what should have happened before police drew weapons on a teenager after a Maryland AI camera mistook a bag of chips for a gun. Finally, he shares why mandates in California and Georgia are racing ahead of testing standards, what an entrance should never be allowed to know about you, and why a 3D printed gun is still not invisible.
